# Omega ratio (`omega_ratio`)

*Category: Risk-adjusted performance · Nature: derived · Unit: ratio · Formula id: `omega_ratio@v1` · Methodology 0.1.0*

## 1. What does it measure?

Probability-weighted gains above the threshold relative to probability-weighted losses below it.

## 2. Formula

```text
sum(max(r_t - L, 0)) / sum(max(L - r_t, 0)), L = 0
```

## 3. Required inputs

Periodic simple returns.

## 4. Is higher or lower better?

Higher is better.

## 5. Plain-language interpretation

Total gains divided by total losses; above 1 means gains outweighed losses.

## 6. Professional interpretation

Keating & Shadwick (2002) Omega at threshold 0, using the full empirical distribution (all moments). Equals 1 + mean / lower partial moment of order 1.

## 7. Assumptions

- Threshold of 0% per period.

## 8. When can it be misleading?

- Few losing periods: the denominator is tiny.
- Compared across data frequencies.

## 9. Minimum sensible data

At least 2 observations and at least one loss; low confidence below 3 years. (policy `ratio_standard`: Risk-adjusted ratios: at least 2 observations; low confidence below 3 years, moderate below 5 years.)

- Keating, C., & Shadwick, W. F. (2002). A Universal Performance Measure. Journal of Performance Measurement, 6(3), 59-84.
- Bacon, C. R. (2021). Practical Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement (2nd ed.). Wiley.

## 12. OpenFactsheet convention

Threshold 0 per period; simple empirical estimator; not annualized.
